title: Granular slice-locks for progressive model promotes with auto-resume rollbacks
author: Maya Chen
description:
Motivation: Progressive model promotes (canaries/A-B/slice-based promos) occasionally expose a mixed-state where some user cohorts see new model variants while others remain on the old model. This can surface cross-slice regressions and complicate rollback. This PR introduces a "slice-lock" concept: a short-lived per-slice lease that pins a slice's requests to a single model variant during promote/handshake, enabling deterministic drain, replay, and a safe resume path on rollback.

Summary of changes: implemented a slice-lock controller in the rollout subsystem, wire up promote and rollback paths to acquire/release locks, added handshake lease renewal (to avoid premature eviction for long-running sessions), added telemetry reconciliation window logic to delay final commit until slice-level metrics are within tolerance, and introduced operator-visible metrics and CLI commands for inspection and manual resume. Also includes integration tests, docs, and CLI helpers.

Design notes: the slice-lock is lease-based (default 30s). During a promote, the controller will: 1) create a promote token and attempt to acquire locks for N target slices based on policy; 2) pin incoming requests for locked slices to the candidate variant while the slice is draining from the old variant; 3) collect slice-level telemetry (latency, error-rate, qa checks) for a configurable reconciliation window (default 3 minutes); 4) if metrics pass, commit the promote and release locks; 5) on metric regressions or operator abort, perform a rollback: the controller triggers a resume that re-acquires locks to steer the slice back to the previous variant while preserving session stickiness.

Safety features: handshake-lease renewal to prevent race during long requests; stale-slice-eviction policy with exponential backoff; quorum-confirmation threshold (percent of slice coverage required before commit) to avoid tiny-sample commits; auto-fallback to global routing when locks cannot be acquired after a timeout.

Backward compatibility: controllers default to disabled for existing rollouts. New rollout policy schema has optional "slice_lock" stanza; older rollout specs continue to work unchanged.

Configuration (new fields): slice_lock.enabled (bool), slice_lock.lease_seconds (int), slice_lock.reconcile_window_seconds (int), slice_lock.quorum_percent (int), slice_lock.eviction_backoff_ms (int).

Testing: unit tests for lock state machine, integration test suite that simulates multi-slice traffic and injected regressions, e2e canary test that runs a staged promote with a deliberate rollback. Notable: integration tests were flaky on first run due to timing assumptions; added wait-for-handshake and explicit clock advances in harness to stabilize.

Rollout plan: feature gated via a cluster config flag. We'll ship docs and a sample rollout manifest in the next minor. Gradual rollout to production tenant groups: start with internal/dev clusters for two weeks, then opt-in beta for projects with slice-based experiments, then broad enable. The rollout controller includes telemetry gates that automatically abort commit if delta thresholds exceed configured SLOs.

Related: builds on prior work for session-affine canaries (ENG-2156) and cohort handoff (ENG-7412). Linear tasks above track followups for UI surface and additional observability.

Checklist: [x] controller implementation; [x] unit tests; [x] integration tests; [x] docs (docs/rollouts/slice-locks.md); [x] CLI inspect/promote helpers; [x] metrics and alerts; [x] changelog entry.
